newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ANTENNA HUNGARIA SELL-OFF NOT ON AGENDA - HORN.
newsitem.headline: ANTENNA HUNGARIA SELL-OFF NOT ON AGENDA - HORN.

text.p: Hungary's prime minister Gyula Horn said on Tuesday the privatisation of broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria Rt, which transmits all of Hungary's national television and radio programmes, was not on the agenda.
"Privatising Antenna Hungaria is not on the government's agenda," Horn told reporters.
Horn was responding to claims made in Parliament that Hungarian-born financier George Soros had been invited to bid for the company.
"George Soros has not presented any indication that he would want to buy Antanna Hungaria if it was to be privatised," Horn added.

Efforts to privatise the company have stalled after its owner, Hungary's state privatisation agency APV, in June declared unsuccessful a new tender to sell a majority stake, rejecting a second bid by the French company Tele Diffusion de France (TDF). TDF last month closed down their Budapest office.

Mihaly T. Revesz, head of the National Radio and Television Authority (ORTT), which is overeseeing the privatisation of Hungary's television and radio last month expressed his misgivings about giving a controlling stake in Antenna Hungaria to a foreign company.
"You don't sell your national stadium and your national team together," he said.
